description:
FILED s525u (Opus, 2026-10-24) while shipping #3760.  PRE-EXISTING for the
arithmetic half (main ef5df65a: `$y += 2.5` under `use integer` = 9.5).

THE GAP.  Pl/ExprToCL.pm's `use integer' block (~:1974) rewrites the BINARY
ops (`/ % + - * & | ^ << >>') to integer forms, but a compound assignment
lowers through %BINARY_OPS / VarAnnotator's compound table to `p-incf`,
`p-<<=`, `p->>=`, `p-bit-and=` ... with no pragma variant, so the pragma is
invisible to the runtime there.

PROBES (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL on the s525u tree):
  use integer; my $y = 7; $y += 2.5; print $y          perl 9      PCL 9.5
  use integer; my $x = -7; $x >>= 1; print $x          perl -4     PCL -4  (the compound keeps the signed shift)
  my $x = -1; $x >>= 1; print $x                       perl 9223372036854775807   PCL -1
  my $x = -1; $x <<= 1; print $x                       perl 18446744073709551614  PCL -2

WHY THE SHIFT PAIR IS HALF-RIGHT ON PURPOSE.  #3760 made `p-<<' / `p->>'
read the left operand as a UV (perl, outside `use integer').  Routing the
compound pair through that would have broken `use integer; $x >>= 1' for a
negative $x (the common case in `use integer' code: hash and PRNG loops), so
`p-<<=' / `p->>=' call %p-shift with SIGNED = T (the pre-#3760 shift).  The
residue is the reverse face: a negative operand of `>>=' / `<<=' OUTSIDE the
pragma.

FIX SHAPE: emit the pragma for the compound family as the binary ops already
do -- `p-<<=-int' / `p->>=-int' (or a flag argument) and integer variants of
`+= -= *= /= %=' under `use integer' -- then drop the SIGNED argument from
the default pair so it delegates to the UV shift.  Emission change: a
generation bump and corpus-diff are part of it.  Guard rows exist:
Pl/t/numify-flag-01.t i02 (the in-pragma compound) pins today's behaviour.


=== DONE (s538a, Opus, 2026-11-12; commit 969453d3, emission, generation v2-13900) ===
Under `use integer` the compound family += -= *= /= %= &= |= ^= <<= >>= lowers to p-op= / p-op=-raw: a GENERIC store
`(p-op= PLACE VALUE (CUR VAL) NEW SLOW)` over the ONE integer table ExprToCL::_integer_op_form (asked by the binary op and
the compound alike), VALUE evaluated before the place is read, the overload guard kept.  `**=`, `++`, `--` have no
integer form in perl (probed).  Outside the pragma `<<=` / `>>=` read a UV like the binary pair (%p-shift's SIGNED flag
and %p-shift-signed deleted) -- the task's two outside-the-pragma probe lines are fixed by the same change.  FOUND on the
way: the pragma rode the Environment scope stack and a named sub's body is lowered before the include statement is reached,
so a file-level `use integer` never reached a sub body (URI::_punycode) and a sub body's own LEAKED to every statement
lowered after it (Math::BigInt::Calc) -- both silent on main.  It is a source-location REGION now
(Pl::Parser::integer_regions_of, the strict-refs shape; a string eval inherits it as pseudo-feature use_integer).  Probes
pr/s3781a.pl + s3781b.pl tree = perl.  Guard Pl/t/numify-flag-01.t i03-i09 (x2 opt), inverse-verified.  ir-spec §10.
BOARD: URI punycode.t (perl 15): base 2 ok / 2 not ok, rc 255 -> 15 / 0 PASS; iri.t (perl 30, 28 + 2 TODO): base 13 / 3 ran 16 ->
24 / 6 to its plan (rows 11 12 13 25 = #1389, 26 29 = TODO, PERL-FAILS).  CLOSE-WITH-ROWS: punycode.t *PLAN* + rows 3 4, iri.t *PLAN*
(#3781) left the board baseline.

ALSO (3781's fallout, found by the full sweep, fixed in the batch): (1) `$#a >>= 1` on an empty array is 2^63-1 since `>>=`
reads a UV, and PCL tried to allocate where perl croaks trappably -- %p-array-extend-check on %p-extend-to (>= 2^61 "Out of
memory during array extend", 2^61-1 "panic: memory wrap"; bop.t's runperl row), guard Pl/t/arylen-ref-01.t row 7; (2)
cl/pack-impl.pl's BER loop `$v >>= 7` relied on the old SIGNED bignum shift -- one encoder _pack_ber = pp_pack.c's UV loop
+ w_string div128 above UV_MAX (pack.t row 10), guard Pl/t/pack-u0-01.t row 3.  Commits e1c99b0c, 25ca3e62, fa425c25.
subject: SILENT WRONG (pre-existing, emission): a COMPOUND assignment ignores `use integer` -- `use integer; my $y = 7; $y += 2.5` is 9 in perl, 9.5 in PCL; and the shift pair `<<=` / `>>=` cannot tell the pragma either, so since #3760 they keep the signed shift everywhere (`my $x = -1; $x >>= 1` is 9223372036854775807 in perl, -1 in PCL)
